meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.text: Два шефа ведут между собой бои.
examples.trans: Two chefs wage battles between themselves.
Are you deceiving me again, chef?
Chef, please hear me out.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('maybe') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maybe you could help?
Maybe tomorrow.
I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be enough', forming an aspectual pair with 'хватать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Chef, maybe that is enough already, huh?
There wasn't enough money.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'already'.

examples.trans: Of course, we finished it a long time ago.
I have already gotten tired of correcting you.
Just get out of here already!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты просто открутил эту штуку!
examples.trans: And you simply unscrewed this thing!

examples.text: А что нам со старой мебелью делать?
examples.trans: And what should we do with the old furniture?

examples.text: А вы закончили вашу дурацкую войну?
examples.trans: And have you finished your foolish war?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('I') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Женщина, не отвлекай, я сейчас проигрываю!
examples.trans: Woman, do not distract me, I am losing right now!

examples.text: Макс, я же тебя просила починить.
examples.trans: Max, I asked you to fix it.

examples.text: Я потом куплю новую и прикручу.
examples.trans: I will buy a new one later and screw it on.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('not') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты полгода резину поменять не можешь.
examples.trans: You have not been able to change the tires for half a year.
You have not finished anything at all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'нимать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to understand', forming an aspectual pair with 'понять'.

examples.text: Я не понимаю, чего вы добиваетесь.
examples.trans: I do not understand what you are trying to achieve.
I understand.
I want to go to the sea, you know?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Max, well, what is this?

examples.text: Делаю то, что должен делать ты.

добиваться.gloss: to strive for, to seek, to court

meanings.en: to strive for, to seek, to court
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (root 'биваться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to strive for', forming an aspectual pair with 'добиться'.

examples.text: Я не понимаю, чего вы добиваетесь.
examples.trans: I do not understand what you are trying to achieve.
You yourself said to court a woman!
So that's what I'm doing.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('but') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Макс, я же тебя просила починить.
examples.trans: Max, I asked you to fix it.
Yes, of course, and just when will that be?

examples.text: Мне же каждый день звонили отсюда.
examples.trans: People called me from here every day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('this') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Max, well, what is this?

examples.text: Я в этом доме и мужчина, и женщина.
examples.trans: In this house I am both the man and the woman.
We will see how you do that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (root 'носить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to bring', forming an aspectual pair with 'принести'.

examples.text: Вам же это не приносит удовольствия.
examples.trans: This does not bring you any pleasure, after all.

examples.text: Я приношу бутылку шампанского и свечи.
examples.trans: I'll bring a bottle of champagne and candles.

examples.text: И не надо больше никаких документов сюда приносить!
examples.trans: And don't bring any more documents in here!

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'pleasure', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Вам же это не приносит удовольствия.
examples.trans: This does not bring you any pleasure, after all.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'red', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: This is red wine, Nastya.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я в этом доме и мужчина, и женщина.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'how much'.

examples.text: Слушай, а сколько можно вас ждать?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (root 'лить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to pour', forming an aspectual pair with 'наливать'.

examples.trans: I said as much as you poured.

examples.trans: I said as much as you poured.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'казать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to say', forming an aspectual pair with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Он бы, наверное, сказал именно так.
examples.trans: He would probably have put it just like this.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'must', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'country', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты должен назвать год и страну.

ошибиться.gloss: to make a mistake, to be mistaken

examples.trans: I will mess up in front of him again.

Sorry, I made a mistake.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in front of' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: I will mess up in front of him again.

There's a car in front of the house.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fine'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Если рыба останется, я вас оштрафую!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to think', forming an aspectual pair with 'подумать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: По-твоему, я зря думаю о семье?
examples.trans: In your opinion, do I think about our family in vain?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'about' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: О, вы стоите рядом и не дерётесь.
examples.trans: Oh, you are standing next to each other and not fighting.

examples.text: По-твоему, я зря думаю о семье?

examples.text: По-твоему, я зря думаю о семье?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('well') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.

examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.
